business_summary.text: Heritage Foods Limited is a leading value-added and branded dairy products company with a presence in 17 states, strong brand affinity, and a vast distribution network. It also has renewable energy generation capacity for captive consumption.

call_points.text: Milk procurement cost rose 11% YoY to ₹47.73/litre in Q2; management expects similar inflation in Q3.
Net weighted average price increase was about 8% in Q2, with September hikes larger and benefits accruing in Q3.
Management declined to speculate on when milk procurement prices will normalise, citing El Niño and supply uncertainty.
EBITDA margin recovered 98 bps sequentially to 5.6% despite high milk costs
Hyderabad ice-cream plant in production, expected at 35-40% utilisation in year one and full over six to seven years.
Paneer and ghee capacity expansion projects are work-in-progress; paneer volumes growing above 30% CAGR.
Cow milk flush has started and volumes are improving, but not yet enough surplus to soften procurement prices.
General trade is ~80% of revenue; modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce ~20%, with comparable margins.
North India and Mumbai regions are still loss-making; FY27 may see some improvement toward breakeven in one region.
Asked whether margins had bottomed, management said it is too early in the season to say.

VAP plus consumer packed fats reached 37.8% of Q4FY25 revenue, up from 34.1% a year ago.
VAP share improved to 35.51% in Q4FY26 from 32.49% in Q4FY25, moving toward the 40% target.
VAP revenue share increased to 35.5% in Q4FY26 from 32.5% YoY
Management now says VAP share will reach ~50% in about four years, versus the earlier 40% in 3-4 years target.
